## Ways to split the work {#landscape}

::: {.cards .two}

::: {.card}
[Task parallelism]{.card-title}
**The inputs:** sweeps, ensembles, many files.

`Pool`, `joblib`, job arrays
:::

::: {.card}
[Data parallelism]{.card-title}
**The data:** map-reduce, split-apply-combine.

`Pool.map` plus combine, `Dask DataFrame`, `Polars`, `Spark`
:::

::: {.card}
[Domain decomposition]{.card-title}
**The space:** grids and meshes, with halo exchange (neighbors swap borders).

`mpi4py`, Dask's `map_overlap`, PETSc via `petsc4py`
:::

::: {.card}
[Pipelines]{.card-title}
**The steps:** stages and queues.

`multiprocessing.Queue`, `Dask`, `Snakemake`, `Nextflow`
:::

:::

## Where the parallelism runs {#landscape-where}

::: {.cards .three}

::: {.card}
[Vectorizing]{.card-title}
**One core:** compiled loops over whole arrays.

`NumPy`, `Numba`
:::

::: {.card}
[Shared-memory threads]{.card-title}
**One process:** threads share memory.

Numba `prange`, NumPy's multithreaded math libraries, the optional free-threaded Python 3.13+
:::

::: {.card}
[Separate processes]{.card-title}
**One machine:** each process has its own memory.

`multiprocessing`, `concurrent.futures`, `joblib`
:::

::: {.card}
[GPUs]{.card-title}
**One GPU:** the data across thousands of cores.

`CuPy`, `PyTorch`, `JAX`
:::

::: {.card}
[Clusters and message passing]{.card-title}
**Many machines.**

`mpi4py`, `Dask`, `Ray`, job arrays
:::

::: {.card .dark}
[Concurrency for waiting]{.card-title}
Not parallel computing, but often confused with it.

`threading`, `asyncio`
:::

:::
